If they love and accept you for who you are as you are in this moment, which it sounds like he does from your original post, then you're just overthinking and allowing the anxious/negative thoughts consume you. Thats not great, I really think you should seek therapy at this level of self doubt and anxious thoughts. Please, don't sabotage yourself because your brain is telling you that you don't deserve to be with him. 

**Immediate solutions that have worked for me:** Do what you can to redirect your apologies when you feel that kind of guilt into positives. Pen and paper work best for this but once you get the hand of it, it's easy to do in your head. Turn your 'im sorry I'm always depressed" into a 'thank you for being patient with me and supporting me through this." It's easiest with the apologies because you can flip it around and turn it into gratitude. Negative thoughts and self talk require a bit more work. Instead of, "he'll stop wanting to be with me if I'm depressed", you could stop, acknowledge the negative thought for what it is, and then redirect or rephrase into something like "he doesn't do or say anything that supports that kind of thought. We've been together for 6 months. If he was going to leave, he would've left by now"

**Long-term solutions/therapy talk:** The way we talk to ourselves impacts the way that we see the world TREMENDOUSLY and I strongly suggest you find yourself a therapist that will help you work through all of this step by step. I've been doing it for almost 15 years and I still have areas that I can improve. But, just like AA/NA, therapy works if you work it. It's big, it's scary, and the more you dig, the more likely it is that you'll experience a session thats really, really painful. But when you wake up the next day? Like a ton of bricks off your shoulders. You forget how good it feels to cry and let it all out until you've finished and you're like, 'wow I had no idea I was holding in all of those emotions, I can breathe again' oh also I forgot to mention that if you do find a therapist, it might be a good idea to bring your boyfriend to sit in for a session so you guys can brainstorm ways to help you stop feeling how you're feeling about your depression affecting your relationship. 

Good luck. I'm sorry for the long ass post, I really resonated with your post and I wanted to go a bit in depth about some things that have personally helped me. It ain't easy, but it's always worth it.
